significance.justification: A verified-true result would establish that after an accepted correction, a "per-item CIE residual" remains separable from stated belief, predictively couples to later misinformation-dependent reasoning, and causally contributes to that behavior because it "can be causally erased"; this combines a form-(iii) predictive relation with a form-(ii) mechanism rather than merely showing that belief is decodable. It would establish both a specific phenomenon—verbal correction acceptance alongside continued reliance—and a mechanism linking the residual representation to that reliance, thereby fixing expectations about which corrected items will still produce errors; Ecker et al. (2022, Nature Reviews Psychology) and Chan et al. (2017, Psychological Science) support the practical importance of distinguishing correction acceptance from subsequent reasoning. Verified false on H1/H2 would informatively rule out this hidden-residual account and support genuine in-context erasure, while failure only of component localization would instead favor a distributed mechanism; these outcomes are distinguishable despite the claim's conjunctive structure. In the topic-substitution check, replacing these specific residual, predictive, and causal assertions with generic "research on LLM beliefs" would not retain this score, because the generic topic supplies neither the dissociation nor the predictive coupling.

reach.justification: The named handles are the "per-item CIE residual," which is a diagnostic predictor, and the contrastive "retraction-completion" steering intervention, which is a corrective knob. The residual is ex ante with respect to the downstream inference error—it is read after the retraction but predicts "continued reliance on the misinformation in downstream inference" before that inference is produced—so an auditor of correction-sensitive RAG or multi-turn systems has an action window. After per-model re-extraction, the substantive residual-to-error predictive coupling and the claimed reduction under stronger explanatory retractions should remain testable predictions, whereas the particular component and steering direction provide only a model-specific procedure and must be rediscovered; scope is a class of in-context retractions and LLMs, with the claim itself acknowledging that transfer to very large closed models is uncertain. The topic-substitution check lowers no credit here: deleting the CIE residual and steering claims leaves the broad belief topic with no predictor, intervention, or pre-error auditing handle.
